scope: One standard-library consumption of the three pinned accepted proof bundles and their SHA-bound existing prediction rows; no model, processor, weights, new QA, rescoring or bootstrap.
findings: The consumer pins the three accepted proof hashes and requires candidate method/backbone identity before reading prediction rows; each prediction SHA, count, ID/order, reference set and original generation cap is checked.
Existing token_f1 scalars are copied and aggregated; no score function is called. S0/acquired/final and all five domains are reported without selecting a successful subset.
The even-sample median now averages the two middle score-token lengths.

Seven fixed nonexclusive literal detectors, answer concentration and acquired-to-final timing have a new use on these complete formal runs; previous limited-cohort image/language/format audits are not rerun.
Public output excludes raw answer/reference text; fixed example selection is written only under OLD .deployment. Cached derived features do not replace the original file SHA check.
limitations: Literal refusal/language/numeric/letter/diversity flags are incomplete descriptive detectors, not certified semantic errors or causes. Low coverage excludes only coverage by these seven rules, not the wider explanations.
Output token count equal to generation cap is not proof of truncation without saved EOS/terminal IDs.
Normalized modal-answer concentration and token-length statistics do not prove semantic collapse; phase alignment does not establish why a change happened.
This is post-hoc sealed TEST failure diagnosis, not permission to select parameters, prompts, modules, models or a new recipe using TEST.
The consumer has a 120-second SIGALRM on OLD; the requested 180-second outer process supervision remains an execution requirement, not an inspected implementation in this two-file review.
The fixed accepted proof hashes were supplied as established provenance; this review does not rerun the original verifier or rehash large model assets.
review_operations: Read only the question and consumer, inspect the three requested fixes, and hash these two local files with the standard library. Did not execute the consumer or import it.
